attributes.body:
In Japanese, なくて is a construction that combines ない (in its conjugation form, なく), with the conjunction particle て. This results in the same 'and' meaning as the standard て form, but with the negative meaning of ない.

なくて is often used when the phrase that comes before it is being highlighted as an example/reason for a specific result. In these situations, the translation is usually 'because not (A), (B)', or 'because I didn't (A), (B)'.

When なくて is used in this way, it is often followed by the speaker's feelings (in the form of an adjective), verbs in the potential form, or something that is generally beyond the control of the speaker. It is due to this fact that the result is 'beyond control' that the translation becomes 'because'.

Some examples of words that express things beyond the control of the speaker are 困（こま）る (to be troubled), 嬉（うれ）しい (to be happy), 疲（つか）れている (to feel weary), 心配（しんぱい） (to feel anxiety/worry), 安心（あんしん） (to feel relief).

attributes.source: [DBJG] A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar

attributes.description: Expressing a sequence of states with the te-form
なくて vs ないで

attributes.body: ないで and なくて are both connecting forms of ない, but with different uses. ないで is used in negative requests or to mean 'without doing' something, e.g. 食べないでください ('Please don't eat it.') and 朝ご飯を食べないで学校に行った ('I went to school without eating breakfast.'). なくて can express a reason or cause, e.g. 行けなくて残念でした ('I couldn't go, which was disappointing.').

second_relatable.meaning: Not ~ and, Not so, Because not (Examples)

attributes.body: Both structures use the て-form to express cause or reason. Verb [て] + B uses the affirmative form to explain a positive reason, e.g. 行けてよかったです ('I'm glad I could go.'). In contrast, なくて is the て-form of the negative ない and expresses a negative reason, e.g. 行けなくて残念でした ('It was unfortunate I couldn't go.').

second_relatable.title: なくて
second_relatable.meaning: Not ~ and, Not so, Because not (Examples)

attributes.body: ではなくて (formal) and じゃなくて (casual) are used with nouns and な-adjectives, while なくて is used with verbs and い-adjectives. Both connect negative forms to another idea and can express cause or reason. For example, 便利じゃなくて残念です ('It's unfortunate it's not convenient.') vs. 行けなくて残念です ('It's unfortunate I couldn't go.').
